evidence: Dimension level: task/tests/scoring.toml:5-11 is '[weights] functional = 0.6 / polish = 0.2 / visual = 0.2', '[floors] functional = 0.05', gates render/constraints = 0.0 (lines 1-3); diff against the frozen template scoring.toml is empty and score.py is byte-identical to the template, so the profile-mandated shares are unchanged. No judge.toml [judge] block carries a weight key (functional judge.toml:1-6, polish:1-6). score.py:41-48 zeros the reward unless every gate passes and functional > 0.05 (strict). Per-criterion weights: Functional has 43 binary criteria summing to 58.5; weights range 0.5-2.5 and track difficulty and brief emphasis. The heaviest (2.5) are hro_stale_refused (refusal naming who moved the card: the brief's declared 'hard part', instruction.md:1-3), hro_live_board (15-second live board, instruction.md:5) and hro_candidate_private ('must never see our internal notes', instruction.md:9). The 2.0 rows cover all-or-none bulk moves, undo restore/conflict, put-back with reason/focus, earlier-page loading, unread counts, scrolled-up notice and drafts, each an explicit brief promise. The lightest (0.5) are basic setup or narrow edge rows: hro_job_open and hro_add_candidate, whose core success is already required by the zero-weight hro_gate_shared, plus hro_reject_hired, hro_undo_full, hro_activity_refusals and hro_candidate_linked. Nothing structural or stylistic sits in Functional. Polish (0.2) has 5 binary behavioural rows summing to 12: live-update preservation of open card/note/focus/scroll (3), thread draft/focus on arrival (3), earlier-page place (2), failed send (1.5), sign-out draft resume and per-user isolation (2.5). These are real brief behaviours (instruction.md:5,7), not cosmetics, so 80 percent of reward mass is functional behaviour and only Visual (0.2; 5 likert-5 rows, equal 1.2 weights, mirroring the template's equal visual weights) is style. Max non-functional contribution: Visual alone is <= 0.2; Polish rows each require working live updates, messaging or sessions, so they cannot be farmed by a shell. Broken app that could pass: a pretty app that only opens jobs and adds candidates (passes both gates) earns 1.0/58.5 = 0.017 functional, which fails the 0.05 floor, so reward = 0. Adding the live board (2.5) clears the floor (3.0/58.5 = 0.051) and gives at most about 0.03 + 0.05 (hro_pol_live_board) + 0.2 visual = 0.28, far below an ugly but fully functional app (>= 0.6). Inverting the order would need strong visual polish against near-zero functionality, which cannot outscore 0.6. Conforming alternative that could fail: weights cannot make a conforming app fail; a criterion-level false negative costs at most 2.5/58.5*0.6 = 2.6 percent, and no single weight dominates. Choices left to the app (drag optional, hidden controls optional, Observer control visibility) are stated as non-penalised in the criteria rather than given weight. Activity, one of three required staff views, carries only 1.5/58.5 (hro_activity 1 + hro_activity_refusals 0.5), about 1.5 percent of reward, but one conjunctive row covers every logged action, so the view's simpler requirement is weighted proportionately. Runtime: raw-evidence-index.json says full configured grading, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent. Row 44 is a source-level weight-design judgement fully decidable from the bytes above.
